Use Python, TypeScript or curl to add a document, wait until the Memory has learned it, and search the result.

This walkthrough adds one note to a Memory, waits for learning to finish, and searches for
what it said. Choose Python, TypeScript or curl; each follows the same sequence.

You need a Membase account, a Memory you can write to, and a working model with available
turns. Create a Memory in the [app quickstart](/use/getting-started/quickstart/)
and check [AI Setup](/use/account-and-models/ai-setup/) if a run cannot use a model.

## 1. Create a key

In the app, open **Connect › Skills › Manage keys › Create key**. Name the key, choose
**Read & write**, and select exactly one Memory under **Memory access** for this walkthrough.
Choose an expiry and create the key. Copy the token while it is shown; it is shown only once.
The profile permission is optional and is not needed for this example.

One Memory matters: no request names a Memory, so a write lands in the key's write target, the
one text Memory it reaches. A key that reaches several is refused with
`422 write_target_required` and nothing is written.

```bash
export MEMBASE_API_KEY="mbk_…"
```

The [key guide](/use/manage-your-memory/connect/#developer-keys) explains rotation and
revocation. The curl example and the SDKs call `https://api.app.membase.com`. Point either SDK
elsewhere with `base_url` / `baseUrl` or `MEMBASE_BASE_URL`.

## 2. Add, wait, then search

`add` returns `202` with a receipt (`{id, kind, status, learning}`) when material is accepted;
it does not promise that learning has finished. Read `documents.get(id)` until every entry of
its `learning` is `succeeded` before searching for the new content. The status is `pending`
while it waits for a run, `processing` while one reads it and `failed` when the run failed. The
examples stop on a failed learning run and have a polling limit, so they cannot wait
indefinitely.


<Tabs syncKey="lang">


<TabItem label="Python">

Install with `pip install unibaseio-membase` (0.4.0 or newer), save this as `quickstart.py`,
and run `python quickstart.py` in the shell where you exported the key.

```python
import time
from membase import Membase

client = Membase()
custom_id = "quickstart-ledger-v1"

added = client.add(
    "We chose Postgres for the Lumen ledger.",
    title="Lumen decision",
    custom_id=custom_id,
)
document_id = added["id"]
if not document_id:
    raise RuntimeError("Accepted, but the document id is pending. See API troubleshooting.")

for _ in range(60):
    learning = client.documents.get(document_id).get("learning") or []
    statuses = {entry["status"] for entry in learning}
    if learning and statuses == {"succeeded"}:
        break
    if "failed" in statuses:
        raise RuntimeError("Learning failed. Open the Memory's Report in the app.")
    time.sleep(5)
else:
    raise TimeoutError("Still unread. Check the Memory's Report and model settings before retrying.")

found = client.search("Which database did we choose for the Lumen ledger?")
errors = [p for p in found["partial"] if p["reason"] == "error"]
if errors:
    raise RuntimeError(f"Some Memories could not answer: {errors}")
for hit in found["items"]:
    print(hit["memory_name"], "·", hit["content"])
if not found["items"]:
    print("No matching passages. Inspect the Memory and its latest Report in the app.")
```

</TabItem>



<TabItem label="TypeScript">

Install with `npm install @unibaseio/membase` (0.4.0 or newer) and run this in a server-side
TypeScript project on Node 18 or newer. The package is ESM-only and the example uses top-level `await`, so the
project must be an ES module: `"type": "module"` in `package.json`, or save the file as
`quickstart.mts`. Keep the key on the server, outside browser bundles.

```ts
import { Membase } from "@unibaseio/membase";

const client = new Membase();
const customId = "quickstart-ledger-v1";
const added = await client.add({
  content: "We chose Postgres for the Lumen ledger.",
  title: "Lumen decision", customId,
});
const documentId = added.id;
if (!documentId) throw new Error("Accepted; document id pending. See API troubleshooting.");
let learned = false;

for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 60; attempt++) {
  const { learning = [] } = await client.documents.get(documentId);
  if (learning.length && learning.every(entry => entry.status === "succeeded")) { learned = true; break; }
  if (learning.some(entry => entry.status === "failed")) {
    throw new Error("Learning failed. Open the Memory's Report in the app.");
  }
  await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 5000));
}
if (!learned) throw new Error("Still unread. Check the Memory's Report and model settings.");

const found = await client.search({ q: "Which database did we choose for the Lumen ledger?" });
const errors = found.partial.filter(p => p.reason === "error");
if (errors.length) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(errors));
for (const hit of found.items) console.log(hit.memory_name, "·", hit.content);
if (!found.items.length) console.log("No matching passages. Inspect the Memory and its Report.");
```

</TabItem>



<TabItem label="curl">

Requires Bash, curl and `jq`. Save this as `quickstart.sh` and run `bash quickstart.sh` in the
shell where you exported the key. A failed HTTP request stops the script.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
BASE=https://api.app.membase.com
AUTH="Authorization: Bearer $MEMBASE_API_KEY"
custom_id=quickstart-ledger-v1
payload=$(jq -n --arg id "$custom_id" \
  '{content: "We chose Postgres for the Lumen ledger.", title: "Lumen decision", custom_id: $id}')
added=$(curl --fail-with-body -sS "$BASE/v1/documents/add" -H "$AUTH" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$payload")
document_id=$(jq -r '.id // empty' <<< "$added")
if [ -z "$document_id" ]; then
  echo "Accepted, but document id pending. See API troubleshooting." >&2
  exit 1
fi
learned=false

for ((attempt=0; attempt<60; attempt++)); do
  document=$(curl --fail-with-body -sS "$BASE/v1/documents/$document_id" -H "$AUTH")
  if jq -e '(.learning | length > 0) and all(.learning[]; .status == "succeeded")' <<< "$document" >/dev/null; then
    learned=true
    break
  fi
  if jq -e 'any(.learning[]; .status == "failed")' <<< "$document" >/dev/null; then
    echo "Learning failed. Open the Memory's Report in the app." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 5
done
if [ "$learned" != true ]; then
  echo "Still unread. Check the Memory's Report and model settings." >&2
  exit 1
fi
payload=$(jq -n '{q: "Which database did we choose for the Lumen ledger?"}')
found=$(curl --fail-with-body -sS "$BASE/v1/search" -H "$AUTH" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$payload")
jq -e 'if any(.partial[]; .reason == "error") then error("A Memory could not answer; inspect partial") else . end' <<< "$found"
```

</TabItem>


</Tabs>


## 3. Check the result

Expect a passage naming Postgres and the Memory it came from. The exact wording can vary.
An empty `items` list is not enough to diagnose a problem: inspect `partial` first (a Memory
named there with `reason: "error"` could not answer), then the Memory's learned content and
latest **Report**.

Re-running this example with the same `custom_id` does not add a second copy: the receipt
names the document already there. If learning was
deferred or failed, fix the cause and run **Update now** in the app; resending the same document
is not a way to force another learning run. See [API troubleshooting](/build/reference/troubleshooting/).
